ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In image1, the same cube is drawn in two different positions. The cube on the left has three visible faces: the top is a small centered square pattern, the front is a pattern horizontally divided into upper and lower halves, and the right face is a centered diamond pattern. The cube on the right has three visible faces: the front is the same small centered square pattern, the top is a 2×2 grid pattern, and the right face is an X-shaped diagonal-line pattern. The clue face in image3 is a large diamond, with the vertices of the diamond close to or reaching the midpoints of the sides of the square. The options in image4 correspond as follows: A is a small diamond, B is a horizontal division, C is a small centered square, D is a 2×2 grid, and E is an X-shape. Reasoning: The small centered square face, that is, option C, is adjacent to the horizontal division face B and the small diamond face A on the left cube; on the right cube, it is adjacent to the 2×2 grid face D and the X-shaped face E. Therefore, this face of option C is already adjacent to four different faces A, B, D, and E. Any face of a cube has only four adjacent faces, so the remaining sixth face must be opposite to it. The remaining face is exactly the large diamond clue face in image3, so the face opposite the clue face is option C.

raw_record.question_text: In the picture above, we see a cube in two different positions. The six sides of the cube are shown. Which side is opposite to the side indicated in the prompt image?

method.method_draft: First read the cube views in image1. The face with a small centered square, corresponding to option C in image4, appears twice: on the top of the left cube and on the front of the right cube. In the left cube this C face touches the horizontally divided face B and the centered-diamond face A. In the right cube this same C face touches the 2-by-2 grid face D and the X face E. Therefore C is adjacent to A, B, D, and E, i.e. to four different faces. A cube face has exactly four adjacent faces, so the only remaining sixth face—the prompt face shown in image3, the large diamond reaching the side midpoints—must be opposite C. Thus the side opposite the prompt image is option C.
